title_candidates: Datasette Agent lets you chat with a real database in your browser
summary: Simon Willison's Datasette Agent adds an AI assistant to SQLite data exploration. A public demo lets you test questions against example databases with a GitHub sign-in.

primary_source.title: Datasette Agent, an extensible AI assistant for Datasette
primary_source.author: Simon Willison
key_facts: Datasette Agent is an open source Datasette plugin that adds an AI assistant for asking questions about SQLite databases.
The official public demo is available at agent.datasette.io and requires GitHub sign-in to reduce abuse.
The demo runs against example databases and can show the SQL used to answer a user's question.
The project launched with plugins for charts, image generation, and sandboxed code execution.
PyPI lists datasette-agent 0.1a4 as a prerelease published on May 24, 2026.

prerequisites: A GitHub account for the public demo sign-in

steps.instruction: Open https://agent.datasette.io/ and confirm the page labels itself as a live demo for exploring SQLite data.
Choose Sign in with GitHub and review the requested access before completing sign-in.
Select one example database shown by the demo and ask a specific question, such as which entries have the highest total or which locations appear most often.
Open the SQL or supporting result shown for the answer and check that the query matches your question.
Use Export Markdown if available to save the conversation and the evidence you checked.
